mcqs.question: What is the definition of linear magnification produced by a thin lens?

options.A: The ratio of the image height to the object height
options.B: The ratio of the object distance to the image distance
options.C: The reciprocal of the focal length of the lens
options.D: The product of the object distance and the image distance

mcqs.answer: The ratio of the image height to the object height
mcqs.explanation: Linear magnification (m) is defined as m = h_i / h_o, where h_i is the image height and h_o is the object height. Option A states this definition. Options B, C and D describe other unrelated quantities.

mcqs.question: A convex lens has a focal length of 0.25 m. What is its optical power?
mcqs.explanation: Power (P) of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length in metres: P = 1/f. Here f = 0.25 m, so P = 1/0.25 = 4 D. Since the lens is convex, the power is positive. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: A concave lens has a focal length of –15 cm. What is its power in dioptres?
mcqs.explanation: First convert the focal length to metres: –15 cm = –0.15 m. Power P = 1/f = 1/(–0.15) = –6.67 D. The negative sign indicates a diverging (concave) lens. Option A matches this value.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses are placed in contact. Lens 1 has a power of +2 D and Lens 2 has a power of –5 D. What is the net power of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: When lenses are in contact, their powers add algebraically: P_total = P1 + P2 = (+2) + (–5) = –3 D. The negative sign shows the combination behaves as a diverging system. Option A is correct.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The statement "The image distance is 20 cm" is:

options.B: False; the correct image distance is 15 cm on the opposite side of the lens
options.C: False; the correct image distance is 20 cm but on the same side as the object
options.D: True; the image forms 20 cm on the same side as the object

mcqs.answer: False; the correct image distance is 15 cm on the opposite side of the lens
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula with Cartesian sign convention: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where u = –30 cm (object on the incoming side) and f = +10 cm. Thus 1/10 = 1/v – 1/30 ⇒ 1/v = 1/10 + 1/30 = 4/30 = 2/15, giving v = +15 cm. The image is real and forms on the opposite side. Therefore the given statement is false, and option B correctly identifies the error.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 12 cm to the left of a concave lens whose focal length is –6 cm. According to the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For a concave lens, f = –6 cm. Object distance u = –12 cm (left side). Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v – 1/u. Substituting, –1/6 = 1/v – (–1/12) ⇒ –1/6 = 1/v + 1/12 ⇒ 1/v = –1/6 – 1/12 = –3/12 = –1/4, so v = –4 cm. The negative sign indicates a virtual image on the same side as the object. Option B is correct.

mcqs.question: An object 5 cm tall is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The same object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave lens of focal length –10 cm. Which statement about the magnifications produced by the two lenses is correct?

options.A: Both lenses produce images of the same magnitude but opposite orientation
options.B: The convex lens produces a real, inverted image with magnification +0.5, while the concave lens produces a virtual, upright image with magnification –0.5
options.C: The convex lens produces magnification +0.5 (upright) and the concave lens produces –0.5 (inverted)
options.D: The convex lens produces magnification –0.5 (inverted) and the concave lens produces +0.5 (upright)

mcqs.answer: The convex lens produces magnification –0.5 (inverted) and the concave lens produces +0.5 (upright)
mcqs.explanation: For the convex lens: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u → 1/10 = 1/v – 1/30 ⇒ v = +15 cm. Magnification m = v/u = 15/(–30) = –0.5 (inverted). For the concave lens: f = –10 cm, u = –30 cm → 1/(–10) = 1/v – 1/(–30) ⇒ 1/v = –1/10 + 1/30 = –2/30 = –1/15 ⇒ v = –15 cm. Magnification m = v/u = (–15)/(–30) = +0.5 (upright). Hence option D correctly describes the signs and orientations.

mcqs.question: In optics, the power of a thin lens is defined as:

options.A: The reciprocal of its focal length measured in metres
options.B: The product of its focal length and the refractive index of the material
options.C: The ratio of the image distance to the object distance
options.D: The difference between the object distance and the image distance

mcqs.answer: The reciprocal of its focal length measured in metres
mcqs.explanation: Power (P) of a lens is given by P = 1/f, where f is the focal length in metres. This definition is standard in competitive examinations. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated quantities.
